title: Mob
text: At that point, it seemed news from the castle town had reached Éclair's parent's ears.
“What did you say!? A Wave in the castle town too!?”
“Yes. Apparently the sky suddenly shifted into some ominous color, and then a tornado of flame burst forth and burned the church to the ground… They say it looked exactly like divine punishment.”
“Hmm…”
Éclair's parent put a hand to the chin, looking thoughtful while listening to Crocodile Guy and his parent, Éclair, and the rest of the group talk it over.
“Could this be a trap?”
Crocodile Guy said warily.
“That's a real possibility. With certain factions of the Three Heroes Church currently running amok… it's difficult either to rush ahead carelessly or to send a messenger to confirm things.”
It seemed they were debating whether to send a guard to check it out.

“‘This isn't a Wave—it's retaliation from those Demi-Humans and Beastmen! Everyone, rise up!’—voices like that are apparently gathering support in the castle town, so… there's a chance it could be dangerous for Seaetto-sama to approach it.”
What was that? Were they really twisting the misfortune of a church getting blown up into something like that?
“What's their basis for that?”
“It happened right after the hourglass started moving again. They're convinced it must be the Demi-Humans and Beastmen's doing, disguised as a Wave…”

Yikes. I'd gone through all that trouble recreating the sky before letting loose, and they still refused to believe it was a Wave? People who make excuses like that will cook up a reason for anything, I say. There's a saying for it in my world too: “logic and salve can stick to anything.” Just then—bang, bang!—someone started pounding on the door of the inn where Éclair's parent was staying.
“Coming.”
When the innkeeper opened the door, there stood a crowd of people, each clutching something that passed for a weapon.
“Is it true that Seaetto, the mastermind who burned down the castle town church, is here!?”
“How dare they pull something like this!”
“I'll kill them!”
This, I believe, is what they call a mob. Wasn't the spread of information—and the damage to Éclair's parent's reputation—happening a bit too fast?
“A-awawa…”
The innkeeper's legs gave out from under him.
“One thing after another, what is this?”
I'd put on that whole display out of irritation to look like divine punishment, and this was how they twisted it?
“We merely stopped here on our way back to the castle. We only just learned of this matter with the Three Heroes Church's cathedral.”
“How shameless of you to say that!”
“This is payback for attacking our church! Dieeeee!”
“Don't mess with us!”

With a clank, Éclair and Crocodile Guy's group drew their weapons, taking a stand against the mob to protect Éclair's parent. Still, watching Éclair's parent get saddled with this much baseless blame, I couldn't help but catch a bit of a resemblance to Father. At the same time, though—weren't they awfully disliked by their own people, considering they'd been championing reconciliation with Siltvelt? Well, given everything that had happened since, I suppose it was a bit late to be surprised. In front of the inn, Éclair and the others clashed with the mob. They were members of the Three Heroes Church, sure, but in the end just small fry—Éclair's side wasn't losing any ground.
“Haaaaaah!”
“Hmph!”

Éclair and Crocodile Guy fought up front, while behind them Éclair's parent and Crocodile Guy's parent dealt with any attacks that slipped through. None of these guys looked particularly skilled. They were, after all, just radical members of the Three Heroes Church. But what should I do here? I could spread status ailments while Hidden, sure… but even then I might get noticed. And even disguised as an usaunny, if I went too wild, I had a feeling I'd be outed as a Hero. Well, unless things got genuinely dangerous, I'd just lurk here and protect them within reasonable limits. As I watched, inside my head Ren and Itsuki chimed in: “That's the mess you caused, isn't it? You get that, right?” No, that's not it at all, I say. Those guys mocked the disaster on Éclair's domain as “divine punishment” and even looted amid the chaos, so I simply delivered the appropriate retribution myself, personally. Calling the disaster on Éclair's domain “divine punishment” while calling the attack on their own church “retaliation” struck me as awfully convenient—though I suppose this was the kind of country where, if they failed to win over me, Itsuki, and Ren, they'd just try to brand us fake Heroes and dispose of us instead.
“Guh, you're saying we can't push through even with these numbers!?”
“Call more reinforcements! Make them pay for burning down the church!”
“Father!”
“Everyone! Fall back!”
At Éclair's cry, Éclair's parent called out too, apparently intending to flee through the inn's back door. With a clatter of footsteps, Éclair's group dashed out the rear and left the town behind.
“Wait! After them!”
“Ohhhh!”

And so the mob gave chase after Éclair's parent as well. Oh? There was a well-dressed fellow in the crowd, grinning smugly. I figured he was the noble mastermind behind all this. Since it ticked me off, I dropped my usaunny form and Hidden status, slipped into the crowd as they ran, and stabbed him. I kept my face hidden under a hood, just in case, I say.
“Gah!?”
“—-sama!? You bastard! What do you think you're doing!”
Oh? Looked like I'd guessed right.
“So this one's the mastermind behind this whole mess?”
“Gh… who are you!”
“That's exactly what I'd like to ask you.”
A murmur rippled through the crowd, and the rioters who'd been whipped into a frenzy froze now that their ringleader, the noble, had suddenly been struck down.
“Let go of me this instant! You! Why are you siding with Seaetto!? Do you intend to bow down to those beasts, our enemies!?”
“Quite lively, aren't you.”

I'd stabbed him on impulse, but maybe I should just blast him away? Hmm… eliminating the witness did seem like a good idea, but the mob's faces made it clear they simply couldn't comprehend that anyone might side with Éclair's parent.
“Death to anyone who sides with Seaetto! Haaaaaah!”
Judging by their movements, it was plain as day these were soldiers posing as civilian rioters, so I swung my spear and used the noble I'd already stabbed as a makeshift club against them.
“Guh!?”
Here's what I'd do: play this off as buying time so Éclair's parent's group could escape. I'd pose as an adventurer swept up by righteous indignation.
“This Seaetto person—was that them just now? What exactly did they do, I wonder?”

“You! A wandering adventurer, are you!? Don't you know!? That one's a grave criminal who invited savage beasts into Melromarc, defied the judgment of divine punishment, and took revenge on the church!”
“Funny, because from where I stood, you lot looked like you were enjoying that chase a little too much. I just stepped in after taking one look at who seemed to be in the right.”
“Outsider! Stay out of this!”
“Hmph!”

Several of them lunged at me, but it wasn't even worth using skills or magic. Levels are merciless, I say. Only a handful had even managed a Class Up, and even those weren't much to speak of. I mowed them all down with a single swing.
“Guaaaaaah!?”
Did they not realize I was only knocking them down, stopping short of killing them? They kept getting back up and attacking again.
“You!”
“Bandit! Get him!”
I'd say you lot are the real bandits here. The way they were so frantically set on killing Éclair's parent over nothing but baseless accusations was downright comical, I say.
“We'll make sure you can't stay in this country anymoreeeee!”
“Hurry up and expose this guy's face! We'll put a bounty on him!”
“Go ahead and try, if you think you can.”
They could be shocked later when my true identity came out. I kept tearing into the mob as they attacked and flinging them aside, over and over.
“Knock it off already, or I'll actually kill you.”
“Go ahead and try—”
With a thud, I drove my spear straight through the forehead of the one who seemed so eager to be killed.
“Agh—”
Twitch! Twitch-twitch! As he convulsed like that, the color drained from the mob's faces one by one.
